h1: The 5 Best Electric Food Choppers Under $50 for Onions, Herbs and Salsa, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Electric Food Chopper Under $50: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 5 electric food choppers aimed at the under $50 shelf, scored on bowl size, motor, blade design and cleanup.
summary: The Ninja Food Chopper Express Chop 200W is the best electric chopper in this price class, with a 200W motor and a 16-ounce bowl for mincing, chopping, grinding and blending. The Cuisinart Mini is the trusted-brand alternative with a reversible blade, the Hamilton Beach 3 Cup is the cheapest, and the BLACK+DECKER is the smallest.
intro: Under $50 you are buying a small motor in a small bowl, and the buying mistake is to expect a food processor. A chopper does onions, garlic, herbs, nuts and salsa in short pulses. It will not shred a block of cheese or slice cucumbers for a salad, and it will stall on a whole raw carrot. Knowing that up front is worth more than any feature list.

Five choppers are ranked below. Four of them list a price bracket at or under $50. The KitchenAid 3.5 cup listing did not confirm a bracket in our data, so check its current price before you buy. Scoring covers bowl size, motor power where listed, blade design and how easy each is to clean.

products.name: Ninja Food Chopper Express Chop 200W
products.verdict: A 200W motor and 16-ounce bowl that minces, chops, grinds and blends.
products.description:
The Express Chop pairs a 200W motor with a 16-ounce bowl, and the listing names mincing, chopping, grinding and blending as its jobs. It sits in the $25 to $50 bracket.

Sixteen ounces is two cups, the right size for an onion or a handful of herbs, and 200W is more motor than the cheapest choppers offer. Grinding makes it useful for spices and coffee beans as well as vegetables. It wins here by being the most capable of the choppers with a firm price tier. The limit is volume: a batch of salsa for a crowd takes two or three runs.

Buy it if you chop small amounts often. Skip it if you cook big batches.

products.name: Cuisinart Mini Food Processor
products.verdict: A 3-cup compact processor with a reversible blade.
products.description:
The Cuisinart Mini offers a 3-cup bowl, a reversible blade and a compact body. It is listed in the $25 to $50 bracket.

The reversible blade has a sharp edge for chopping and a blunt one for mixing and grinding, so one blade covers two jobs. Three cups is larger than the Ninja's bowl, which lets you make a small batch of dip in one go. It ranks second because the listing omits motor power, so you rely on the Cuisinart name.

Buy it if you want a bigger bowl from a respected brand. Skip it if you want a stated wattage.
products.idealFor: Dips and sauces in small batches.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 1.5-Cup Electric Food Chopper
products.verdict: A 150W, 1.5-cup chopper with one-touch pulse, a stay-sharp blade and dishwasher-safe parts.
products.description:
The BLACK+DECKER is a 150W chopper with a 1.5-cup bowl, one-touch pulse, a stay-sharp blade and dishwasher-safe parts. It sits in the under $25 bracket.

One-touch pulse is the control that matters, since it lets you chop in bursts and stop before everything turns to paste. Dishwasher-safe parts remove the main reason people stop using small choppers: the awkward hand-wash. It ranks third because 1.5 cups and 150W are modest.

Buy it if you want an inexpensive, easy-clean chopper. Skip it if you want more bowl or power.

products.name: Hamilton Beach 3 Cup Electric Vegetable Chopper
products.verdict: A 3-cup electric mini processor in the lowest price bracket.
products.description:
The Hamilton Beach 3 Cup is an electric vegetable chopper that works as a mini food processor, in the under $25 bracket.

Three cups of capacity at the lowest price is the draw. It ranks fourth because the listing gives no motor power, blade design or cleaning detail, so the case rests on size and cost. Hamilton Beach is a mainstream brand with easy-to-find replacement bowls.

Buy it if you want the most capacity for the least money. Skip it if you want listed power.
pros: Three cup bowl at a low price
products.idealFor: Big mini-bowl capacity on a budget.

products.name: KitchenAid 3.5 Cup Food Chopper KFC3516CU
products.verdict: A 3.5-cup chopper in Contour silver; check the current price against your $50 limit.
products.description:
The KFC3516CU is a 3.5-cup chopper in Contour silver from KitchenAid. Our data did not confirm its price bracket, so check the current price before treating it as a sub-$50 option.

The larger 3.5 cup bowl is the biggest of the choppers here, and the silver finish suits a stainless kitchen. It ranks last because the price is unconfirmed and the listing gives no motor or blade information.

Buy it if the price lands under $50 and you want a KitchenAid. Skip it if you are strict on budget.
products.idealFor: A KitchenAid look in a compact size.

whatMatters.detail: A 16-ounce bowl is two cups, enough for one onion. Three cups handles a small dip. Choose a bowl about twice your normal batch to avoid repeat runs.
A pulse button lets you chop in bursts and keep texture. Without it, onions go from chunky to mush in seconds. One-touch pulse, as on the BLACK+DECKER, is the best control at this price.
A 200W motor chops soft vegetables and nuts but struggles with dense roots. Many listings omit wattage. Cut hard vegetables into small pieces for any chopper.
A stay-sharp blade resists dulling, and a reversible blade offers a second edge for grinding. Both extend the life of a cheap chopper.
Dishwasher-safe bowls and lids make daily use easy. Blades usually need a careful hand wash. Check which parts can go in the dishwasher.

faq.q: Can a mini chopper handle carrots?
faq.a: Yes, if cut into small pieces first. Whole carrots can stall a 150W or 200W motor. Add them in small amounts.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying one?
faq.a: Expecting slicing and shredding. Choppers have one blade and chop only. If you need discs, consider a processor.

faq.q: Is the Ninja worth it over the BLACK+DECKER?
faq.a: If you grind spices or chop tougher vegetables, yes. The BLACK+DECKER is cheaper and easier to clean.
Pulse in short bursts and stop to check. Cut ingredients into even chunks before they go in.

faq.q: Are the blades sharp when handling?
faq.a: Yes. Remove the blade carefully by the plastic hub and wash by hand. Never put fingers near the cutting edge.
Avoid it unless the maker says so. Ice dulls blades and stresses small motors.

finalTake: The Ninja Food Chopper Express Chop 200W is the best electric food chopper in this price class, with the strongest motor and a bowl suited to daily mincing. The Cuisinart Mini adds a reversible blade and a larger bowl, and the BLACK+DECKER is the easiest to clean. Check the KitchenAid's current price before treating it as a sub-$50 option.
